The Householder
HOWS-hohl-der
noun phrase
From the Greek oikodespotes, “master of a house,” the instructed scribe of the Lord’s parable who brings forth treasure new and old.

Biblical Definition

The parable of the householder, the briefest of the Lord’s kingdom parables, sets forth the instructed disciple as a steward of divine truth. When the Lord had spoken the parables of the kingdom and asked, Have ye understood all these things? they said unto Him, Yea, Lord. Then said He unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old (Mat 13:52). The dictionary marks this householder as the picture of every faithful teacher in the church, the scribe taught of God, whose mind is a treasury furnished from the Scriptures. He brings forth things old, the law and the prophets, the ancient revelation of the LORD; and things new, the gospel of the kingdom now opened in Christ; and he shows the two to be one treasure, for the new is the fulfilling of the old, and the old is the promise of the new. So the Scripture teaches that the minister of the word is no mere reservoir but a dispenser, bringing forth from his store as the household has need. He is instructed unto the kingdom, taught by the Spirit to understand and to teach; and his treasure is not his own invention but the deposit of truth committed to him, old and new together, that he may feed the people of God with the whole counsel of the LORD.

Webster 1828 Definition

The Lord’s parable of the instructed scribe, likened to a householder bringing treasure new and old.

THE HOUSEHOLDER, the Lord’s parable of the instructed scribe of the kingdom.

Every scribe instructed unto the kingdom is like a householder.

He bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

The old is the law and prophets; the new is the gospel of the kingdom.

He is a steward dispensing the whole counsel of God.

Key Scripture

Mat 13:52 — "Then said he unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old."

Mat 13:51 — "Jesus saith unto them, Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea, Lord."

2Ti 2:15 — "Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth."

Mat 13:11 — "He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given."

Modern Corruption

A parable of Scripture; it sets forth the instructed teacher as a steward bringing forth from his treasure things new and old.

expand to see more

The householder has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as the Lord’s figure of the instructed scribe of the kingdom. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the office of the faithful teacher, whose treasure is the whole counsel of God.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the minister of the word is a steward bringing forth out of his treasure things new and old. The scribe instructed unto the kingdom holds the old, the law and the prophets, and the new, the gospel now opened in Christ, and shows them to be one treasure, the new fulfilling the old and the old promising the new. He is no mere reservoir but a dispenser, feeding the household as it has need. So the parable teaches that sound teaching is not invention but the faithful bringing forth of the deposit of truth committed to the church, rightly divided for the people of God.
